findings: Species identity is correct: the dark brown-black plumage, bronzy scaled-looking coverts, long kinked neck, heavy body, hooked bill, orange-yellow facial skin, aquamarine eye, large webbed feet, broad wing, and long wedge-shaped tail agree with the reference photographs and live identification sources.
The illustrated bird has one head, one beak, two wings, two legs, and one tail; the detached head and wing are clearly supplementary studies rather than extra attached anatomy.

The common name, current scientific name Nannopterum auritum, family Phalacrocoracidae, measurements, habitat, behavior, and all listed field marks are supported by the verification sources. No material factual or spelling errors were found.
The absence of paired head crests is valid for a nonbreeding adult, although the plate does not label the plumage stage or mention that the namesake crests appear only during breeding season.
Minor composition issue: the ruler-like graphic has no units or numerical labels and therefore cannot communicate an actual scale.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
